---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>
Date: Wed, Dec 17, 2014 at 2:24 PM
Subject: Re: BioGeoBEARS outputs
To: Lukas Ruber <lukas...@nmbe.ch>

Hi!  Thanks for the question.

Yes, it's even easier than Lagrange to get the probabilities of each ancestral state. E.g. if the result object is "res", they are stored in the listed elements in "res":

names(res)

E.g. the probabilities of each states at each node are in:

res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node

The probabilities of each state at each "corner" (branch bottom, representing the states instantaneously after cladogenesis splits) are in:

res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node

These tables have:

rows: tips, then root node, then internal nodes -- numbered as in the APE package defaults or the prt() function

columns: states (each state is a geographic range, e.g. for 2 areas there are 4 states/ranges: null, A, B, or AB

See e.g.: http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#node_numbering

Note that these are the state probabilities under the global ML model. Lagrange does state probabilities slightly differently, by fixing each ancestral state at each node and re-optimizing the model parameters under each constraint. They are typically similar but there can be some differences. See Matzke 2014, Sys Bio.

Cheers!  Hope it works for you, let me know how it goes.

Nick

PS: Can I post this answer to the BioGeoBEARS google group?  It will help other people...
